objective: Prevent unintended queue consumption during production bring-up: the scheduled claim sweep (cron '* * * * *' on .github/workflows/factoryos-render-worker.yml) is now gated behind a non-secret repo variable RENDER_WORKER_SCHEDULER_ENABLED=1, while workflow_dispatch stays always-allowed so the owner can validate the credential handshake one controlled job at a time. Root cause of the current scheduled failures was verified from the workflow's own annotation, not inferred: 'RENDER_WORKER_SECRET is not configured; refusing to claim a job.' (fail-closed guard from PR #247, run 39913423934).

security.notes: Change is a job-level scheduling gate only: no new input surfaces, no trigger added, no secret logic touched; claim/callback fail-closed behavior unchanged. The gate reduces risk (prevents auto-claim of queued jobs before provider/storage verification). No secrets printed or committed.

blockedReason: Live production acceptance requires owner-only actions: revoke the exposed PAT; rotate RENDER_WORKER_SECRET and FACTORYOS_EXECUTION_SECRET; configure GITHUB_RENDER_TOKEN; supply LIGHTNING_API_KEY/LIGHTNING_USER_ID and provider credentials; confirm MongoDB and durable CAS/storage; choose a Node runtime lane for the SQLite-backed stores. Queue contents cannot be inspected read-only (claim-only API by contract); no queue request is emitted while the secret is unconfigured, so no unintended work can start during bring-up preparation.
